Ajustado: el tamaño sale bien; la forma depende del viento. Preliminar, sin calibrar

Parafire · Simulación de incendios · INFONA
Notas
  • Qué es: el componente que, desde un punto de ignición, estima cómo se comporta el fuego (velocidad, intensidad, llama) y hacia dónde se propaga.
  • Con qué: Pyretechnics para comportamiento (Rothermel) y propagación (level set), grilla de 100 m en UTM 21S.
  • Ronda 1: en abiertos el ajuste corrige el tamaño también en incendios reservados; la superposición no mejora y se explica principalmente por el viento (r = -0.87). En bosque el ajuste no generaliza.

Parafire · Simulación de incendios · INFONA
Notas
  • Scott & Burgan (2005, RMRS-GTR-153) definen 40 modelos estándar; cada uno fija carga por tamaño, profundidad, humedad de extinción y calor.
  • El número dentro de cada familia sube con la carga (GR1 poca, GR9 mucha); clima seco o húmedo cambia la humedad de extinción.
  • Pyretechnics acepta 58 códigos: Anderson 13, Scott & Burgan 40 y no combustibles. Antes de cada corrida se comprueba que todos los códigos del mapa estén en esa tabla; si falta uno, la corrida no arranca.

Parafire · Simulación de incendios · INFONA
Notas
  • Leñosas cerradas → TU5. Scott & Burgan 2005 (RMRS-GTR-153) TU5 = very high load, dry-climate timber-shrub: heavy forest litter under a shrub or small-tree understory carries the fire (moderate spread, moderate flame length). This fits Chaco dry forest (quebrachal), which has a dense thorny shrub layer, terrestrial bromeliads (caraguatá) and deep deciduous litter in the dry season. The pilot areas are Chaco, so V01 picks the Chaco reading. The class also covers humid Atlantic (Alto Paraná) forest, where TU5 overstates fire behaviour.
  • Pastura → GR2. Cultivated forage pasture (in the Chaco: gatton panic, buffel grass, Brachiaria), usually grazed. S&B GR2 = low-load dry-climate grass: grass is the carrier, shrubs (if any) do not affect behaviour, high spread rate, moderate flame length. Grazing keeps the load low. This class is sensitive: ungrazed gatton panic can carry far more fuel.
  • Leñosas inundables → TU3. The official definition covers trees, shrubs and palm savannas (palmares, e.g. karanday) that depend on flooding. S&B TU3 = moderate-load humid-climate timber-grass-shrub: forest litter with grass and shrub components and high extinction moisture (30 %), high spread rate, moderate flame length. That combination of grass layer, woody component and humid climate fits.
  • Pastizales inundables → GR6. Esteros, bañados and cañadas: natural herbaceous vegetation that depends on flooding. S&B GR6 = moderate-load humid-climate grass (fuelbed depth 1.5 ft, extinction moisture 40 %; very high spread rate, high flame length). The humid-climate grass models fit vegetation that only burns once the wetland dries out. A moderate load is chosen because the class also includes short wet meadows.
  • Pastizal → GR4. Natural grassland (Chaco espartillares and pajonales, campos) where woody cover is under ~20 %. S&B GR4 = moderate-load dry-climate grass: continuous, coarse grass about 2 ft deep, high spread rate, moderate flame length. Grass is the primary carrier.
  • Leñosas abiertas → GS2. With 15–65 % woody canopy, enough light reaches the ground for grass and shrubs to carry the fire. S&B GS2 = moderate-load dry-climate grass-shrub: shrubs 1–3 ft with moderate grass, high spread rate, moderate flame length. This matches Chaco and Cerrado savanna woodland and open quebrachal.
  • Forestaciones → TL6. Tree plantations, mostly eucalyptus in the Región Oriental, plus pine and fruit or citrus orchards. S&B TL6 = moderate-load broadleaf litter (less compact than TL2), moderate spread rate, low flame length. Eucalyptus leaf and bark litter is the main surface carrier in managed stands.
  • Borrador técnico (V01 DRAFT); espera el análisis y la validación del equipo de combustibles.

Ojo: el rastrojo de cultivo sí arde en la seca.

Parafire · Simulación de incendios · INFONA
Notas
  • Agricultura → NB3. Annual grain and fibre crops (soy, maize, wheat). S&B NB3 = agricultural field maintained in a non-burnable condition. Green crops and tilled fields act as firebreaks in spread simulation. Alternativas: GR1 (101, short sparse dry-climate grass) for post-harvest stubble in the dry season; GR2 (102) for fallow fields. Consider a seasonal rule in V02.
  • Ríos, lagos y océano → NB8. Open water. S&B NB8 = open water (non-burnable). The engine's source comment labels code 98 'NB4'; Scott & Burgan call it NB8. Alternativas: None.
  • Áreas sin vegetación → NB9. Built-up areas, roads, quarries and natural bare surfaces (outcrops, sand banks, salt flats). The S&B NB codes are behaviourally identical in the engine: all are non-burnable with zero load. NB9 (bare ground) is picked because in the Chaco most class-25 pixels are roads, bare soil and salt flats. The engine's source comment labels code 99 'NB5'; Scott & Burgan call it NB9. Alternativas: NB1 (91, urban/developed) for towns. Behaviour is identical; it only changes the label.
  • Para la V02: regla estacional para agricultura (GR1 o GR2 en rastrojo, NB3 con cultivo verde).

Parafire · Simulación de incendios · INFONA
Notas
  • Leñosas cerradas: TU2 (162, moderate-load humid-climate timber-shrub) for Atlantic forest in the Región Oriental; TL6 (186, moderate broadleaf litter) where the understory is sparse; SH7 (147, very high load dry-climate shrub) for degraded Chaco thicket (fachinal); TU1 (161) as a lighter option. V02 should split this class by ecoregion.
  • Pastura: GR4 (104) for lightly grazed pasture; GR7 (107) for ungrazed tall gatton panic at the end of the dry season; GS2 (122) for pasture invaded by woody regrowth (renoval).
  • Leñosas inundables: GS3 (123, moderate-load humid-climate grass-shrub) for open palm savanna; GS4 (124) for tall, dense palm savanna; TL6 (186) for closed gallery or riparian forest.
  • Pastizales inundables: GR8 (108, high-load very coarse humid-climate grass, 4–5 ft) for tall paja brava or sedge esteros; GR9 (109) for very tall dense stands (Pantanal/Chaco wetlands in drought years); GR5 (105) for short wet meadows; GS3 (123) where shrubs are present.
  • Pastizal: GS2 (122) where woody cover approaches 20 %; GR2 (102) for heavily grazed grassland; GR7 (107, high-load dry-climate grass) for tall dense ungrazed stands.
  • Leñosas abiertas: TU1 (161, low-load dry-climate timber-grass-shrub) if litter under trees dominates; SH2 (142) for shrub-dominated open woodland; GR4 (104) for grass-dominated savanna.
  • Forestaciones: TL3 (183) or TL8 (188) for pine plantations; TU1 (161) for young plantations with a grass understory; GR2 (102) for orchards with grazed or mowed grass.

Cómo medimos

IoU: cuánto coinciden la simulación y la cicatriz real

IoU = área quemada por los dos ÷ área quemada por cualquiera

Cicatriz real (MapBiomas Fuego)Simulación
  • 1 = idénticas; 0 = no se tocan.
  • Castiga tanto lo que falta como lo que sobra.

IoU 0.80

Lugar y tamaño correctos

IoU 0.25

Tamaño correcto, empujado hacia otro lado

IoU 0.50

Lugar correcto, el doble de grande

IoU 0.50

Lugar correcto, la mitad de grande

Dónde están hoy nuestros resultados (mediana en combustibles abiertos; el piloto es un solo incendio).

Parafire · Simulación de incendios · INFONA
Notas
  • IoU = intersección sobre unión (intersection over union). Se cuenta en celdas de 100 m: celdas quemadas por ambos ÷ celdas quemadas por al menos uno.
  • Un incendio perfectamente ubicado pero del doble o de la mitad del tamaño ya baja a 0,50: por eso tamaño y lugar se miran juntos.
  • Muchos estudios publican el índice de Sørensen en lugar de IoU: Sørensen = 2 × IoU ÷ (1 + IoU). IoU 0,50 equivale a Sørensen 0,67.
  • Los incendios vecinos que ardieron a la vez se excluyen de la cicatriz antes de puntuar.
  • La IoU no dice nada del ritmo: un incendio puede terminar en el lugar correcto habiendo crecido a destiempo.
Cómo medimos

Cada medida responde una pregunta distinta

MedidaPregunta que respondeCómo se lee
IoU¿Quemó el lugar correcto?0 a 1; 1 = idéntica a la cicatriz
Tamaño (× observado)¿Quemó la cantidad correcta?simulado ÷ real; 1× = igual; «tamaño correcto» = entre 0,5× y 2×
Crecimiento vs casco VIIRS¿Creció al ritmo correcto?área simulada a la hora de cada pasada del satélite
Error de dirección (°)¿Empujó el viento hacia el lado correcto?ángulo entre el viento ERA5 y la dirección ignición → centro de la cicatriz; 0° = igual, 180° = al revés
Mediana¿Qué resultado es típico?el incendio del medio al ordenarlos
Entrenamiento / reservados¿Funciona con incendios nuevos?se elige con unos incendios y se juzga con otros
Correlación (r)¿Se mueven juntas dos cosas?−1 a 1; 0 = sin relación
Sesgo y error medio (RMSE)¿ERA5 se parece a la estación?sesgo = diferencia promedio; RMSE = tamaño típico del error, en las unidades de la variable
How this panel was checked
  • Pase el cursor por «Cómo se lee» para ver el detalle y dónde se usa.

Ninguna medida sola alcanza: lugar, tamaño y ritmo se leen juntos.

Ningún giro fijo del viento ayuda, y las estaciones MCH no están más cerca que ERA5.

Parafire · Simulación de incendios · INFONA
Notas
  • Corridas en Aurora (servidor de NCEAS): unas 2.000 simulaciones por minuto.
  • Encender desde la huella VIIRS agranda los incendios (~1,45× a velocidad ×0,4); con ×0,35 quedan en ~1,2× y mantienen la mejora en reservados.
  • Estaciones MCH: 15 incendios con una estación a menos de 75 km; error de dirección mediano 43° (estación) contra 40° (ERA5).
  • Códigos por ecorregión, juzgados dejando un incendio afuera por vez: en el Chaco seco empeoran (0,30 → 0,23); en el Chaco húmedo empatan con una simple reducción de velocidad (×0,35). No se adoptan.
  • Señal estable en el Chaco húmedo, para el equipo de combustibles: pastizal → GR2 y pastura → GR3 en los 20 pliegues; bosque → TU2 en 17.
  • Configuración provisional para diciembre: la de la ronda 1 más encendido desde la huella VIIRS y velocidad ×0,35. No validada.

Notes
  • What it is: the component that, from an ignition point, estimates how the fire behaves (spread rate, intensity, flame length) and where it spreads.
  • With what: Pyretechnics for behaviour (Rothermel) and spread (level set), on a 100 m grid in UTM 21S.
  • Round 1: in open fuels tuning fixes size on held-out fires too; overlap does not improve and is mostly explained by wind (r = -0.87). In forest tuning does not generalise.

Scott & Burgan: fuel families

🌾 GR · Grass

grass carries the fire · 9 models

🌿 GS · Grass-shrub

grass with low shrubs · 4 models

🌳 SH · Shrub

shrubs dominate · 9 models

🌲 TU · Timber-understory

litter + grass/shrub under trees · 5 models

🍂 TL · Timber litter

only the litter burns · 9 models

🚫 NB · Non-burnable

water, crops, bare ground · 5 models

Each land-cover class gets one code from this table.

Parafire · Fire simulation · INFONA
Notes
  • Scott & Burgan (2005, RMRS-GTR-153) define 40 standard models; each fixes load by size class, depth, moisture of extinction and heat.
  • The number within a family rises with load (GR1 little, GR9 a lot); dry vs humid climate changes the moisture of extinction.
  • Pyretechnics accepts 58 codes: Anderson 13, Scott & Burgan 40 and non-burnables. Before every run each code on the map is checked against that table; if one is missing, the run does not start.

Each land cover, one fuel model

Burnable classes cover 90% of the country; 61% has low confidence.

Parafire · Fire simulation · INFONA
Notes
  • Closed Natural Woodlands → TU5. Scott & Burgan 2005 (RMRS-GTR-153) TU5 = very high load, dry-climate timber-shrub: heavy forest litter under a shrub or small-tree understory carries the fire (moderate spread, moderate flame length). This fits Chaco dry forest (quebrachal), which has a dense thorny shrub layer, terrestrial bromeliads (caraguatá) and deep deciduous litter in the dry season. The pilot areas are Chaco, so V01 picks the Chaco reading. The class also covers humid Atlantic (Alto Paraná) forest, where TU5 overstates fire behaviour.
  • Pasture → GR2. Cultivated forage pasture (in the Chaco: gatton panic, buffel grass, Brachiaria), usually grazed. S&B GR2 = low-load dry-climate grass: grass is the carrier, shrubs (if any) do not affect behaviour, high spread rate, moderate flame length. Grazing keeps the load low. This class is sensitive: ungrazed gatton panic can carry far more fuel.
  • Flooded Natural Woodlands → TU3. The official definition covers trees, shrubs and palm savannas (palmares, e.g. karanday) that depend on flooding. S&B TU3 = moderate-load humid-climate timber-grass-shrub: forest litter with grass and shrub components and high extinction moisture (30 %), high spread rate, moderate flame length. That combination of grass layer, woody component and humid climate fits.
  • Flooded grasslands → GR6. Esteros, bañados and cañadas: natural herbaceous vegetation that depends on flooding. S&B GR6 = moderate-load humid-climate grass (fuelbed depth 1.5 ft, extinction moisture 40 %; very high spread rate, high flame length). The humid-climate grass models fit vegetation that only burns once the wetland dries out. A moderate load is chosen because the class also includes short wet meadows.
  • Grassland → GR4. Natural grassland (Chaco espartillares and pajonales, campos) where woody cover is under ~20 %. S&B GR4 = moderate-load dry-climate grass: continuous, coarse grass about 2 ft deep, high spread rate, moderate flame length. Grass is the primary carrier.
  • Open Natural Woodlands → GS2. With 15–65 % woody canopy, enough light reaches the ground for grass and shrubs to carry the fire. S&B GS2 = moderate-load dry-climate grass-shrub: shrubs 1–3 ft with moderate grass, high spread rate, moderate flame length. This matches Chaco and Cerrado savanna woodland and open quebrachal.
  • Forest Plantation → TL6. Tree plantations, mostly eucalyptus in the Región Oriental, plus pine and fruit or citrus orchards. S&B TL6 = moderate-load broadleaf litter (less compact than TL2), moderate spread rate, low flame length. Eucalyptus leaf and bark litter is the main surface carrier in managed stands.
  • Technical draft (V01 DRAFT); waiting on the fuels team's analysis and validation.
Fuels · crosswalk

What does not burn

Land cover% of ParaguayCodeWhy
Agriculture8%NB3 agricultural, non-burnableGreen or tilled crops act as firebreaks
River, Lake and Ocean1%NB8 open waterWater
Non vegetated areas0.7%NB9 bare groundNo vegetation

Caveat: crop stubble does burn in the dry season.

Parafire · Fire simulation · INFONA
Notes
  • Agriculture → NB3. Annual grain and fibre crops (soy, maize, wheat). S&B NB3 = agricultural field maintained in a non-burnable condition. Green crops and tilled fields act as firebreaks in spread simulation. Alternatives: GR1 (101, short sparse dry-climate grass) for post-harvest stubble in the dry season; GR2 (102) for fallow fields. Consider a seasonal rule in V02.
  • River, Lake and Ocean → NB8. Open water. S&B NB8 = open water (non-burnable). The engine's source comment labels code 98 'NB4'; Scott & Burgan call it NB8. Alternatives: None.
  • Non vegetated areas → NB9. Built-up areas, roads, quarries and natural bare surfaces (outcrops, sand banks, salt flats). The S&B NB codes are behaviourally identical in the engine: all are non-burnable with zero load. NB9 (bare ground) is picked because in the Chaco most class-25 pixels are roads, bare soil and salt flats. The engine's source comment labels code 99 'NB5'; Scott & Burgan call it NB9. Alternatives: NB1 (91, urban/developed) for towns. Behaviour is identical; it only changes the label.
  • For V02: a seasonal rule for agriculture (GR1 or GR2 on stubble, NB3 with a green crop).

Calibration tests these alternatives against real scars.

Parafire · Fire simulation · INFONA
Notes
  • Closed Natural Woodlands: TU2 (162, moderate-load humid-climate timber-shrub) for Atlantic forest in the Región Oriental; TL6 (186, moderate broadleaf litter) where the understory is sparse; SH7 (147, very high load dry-climate shrub) for degraded Chaco thicket (fachinal); TU1 (161) as a lighter option. V02 should split this class by ecoregion.
  • Pasture: GR4 (104) for lightly grazed pasture; GR7 (107) for ungrazed tall gatton panic at the end of the dry season; GS2 (122) for pasture invaded by woody regrowth (renoval).
  • Flooded Natural Woodlands: GS3 (123, moderate-load humid-climate grass-shrub) for open palm savanna; GS4 (124) for tall, dense palm savanna; TL6 (186) for closed gallery or riparian forest.
  • Flooded grasslands: GR8 (108, high-load very coarse humid-climate grass, 4–5 ft) for tall paja brava or sedge esteros; GR9 (109) for very tall dense stands (Pantanal/Chaco wetlands in drought years); GR5 (105) for short wet meadows; GS3 (123) where shrubs are present.
  • Grassland: GS2 (122) where woody cover approaches 20 %; GR2 (102) for heavily grazed grassland; GR7 (107, high-load dry-climate grass) for tall dense ungrazed stands.
  • Open Natural Woodlands: TU1 (161, low-load dry-climate timber-grass-shrub) if litter under trees dominates; SH2 (142) for shrub-dominated open woodland; GR4 (104) for grass-dominated savanna.
  • Forest Plantation: TL3 (183) or TL8 (188) for pine plantations; TU1 (161) for young plantations with a grass understory; GR2 (102) for orchards with grazed or mowed grass.

How we score

IoU: how well the simulation matches the real scar

IoU = area burned by both ÷ area burned by either

Real scar (MapBiomas Fuego)Simulation
  • 1 = identical; 0 = no overlap.
  • It penalises both missed and extra area.

IoU 0.80

Right place, right size

IoU 0.25

Right size, pushed the wrong way

IoU 0.50

Right place, twice too big

IoU 0.50

Right place, half too small

Where our results are today (median in open fuels; the pilot is a single fire).

Parafire · Fire simulation · INFONA
Notes
  • IoU = intersection over union. It is counted on 100 m cells: cells burned by both ÷ cells burned by at least one.
  • A perfectly placed fire that is twice or half the size already drops to 0.50: so size and place are read together.
  • Many studies report the Sørensen index instead of IoU: Sørensen = 2 × IoU ÷ (1 + IoU). IoU 0.50 equals Sørensen 0.67.
  • Neighbouring fires that burned at the same time are removed from the scar before scoring.
  • IoU says nothing about timing: a fire can end in the right place after growing at the wrong pace.
How we score

Each measure answers a different question

MeasureQuestion it answersHow to read it
IoUDid it burn the right place?0 to 1; 1 = identical to the scar
Size (× observed)Did it burn the right amount?simulated ÷ real; 1× = equal; 'sized right' = between 0.5× and 2×
Growth vs VIIRS hullDid it grow at the right pace?simulated area at the time of each satellite pass
Direction error (°)Did the wind push the right way?angle between ERA5 wind and the ignition → scar-centre direction; 0° = same, 180° = opposite
MedianWhat is a typical result?the middle fire when sorted
Training / held outDoes it work on new fires?chosen on some fires, judged on others
Correlation (r)Do two things move together?−1 to 1; 0 = no relation
Bias and RMSEDoes ERA5 match the station?bias = average difference; RMSE = typical error size, in the variable's units
How this panel was checked
  • Hover over 'How to read it' for the detail and where it is used.

No single measure is enough: place, size and pace are read together.

Parafire · Fire simulation · INFONA
Notes
  • Every measure compares against satellite observations (MapBiomas Fuego and VIIRS), not field measurements.
  • Spread rate, intensity and flame length cannot be validated with these data; only the final footprint and the growth.

How this panel was checked
  • Same fires in every bar (20 training, 9 held out); round-1 frozen split.
  • 'Perfect wind' turns the ERA5 wind toward where the real fire went: it is a ceiling, not usable in operations.

No fixed wind rotation helps, and MCH stations are no closer than ERA5.

Parafire · Fire simulation · INFONA
Notes
  • Runs on Aurora (the NCEAS server): about 2,000 simulations a minute.
  • Igniting from the VIIRS footprint makes fires bigger (~1.45× at spread ×0.4); at ×0.35 they are ~1.2× and keep the held-out gain.
  • MCH stations: 15 fires with a station within 75 km; median direction error 43° (station) against 40° (ERA5).
  • Codes by ecoregion, judged leaving one fire out at a time: in the dry Chaco they make results worse (0.30 → 0.23); in the humid Chaco they tie with a simple spread reduction (×0.35). Not adopted.
  • Stable signal in the humid Chaco, for the fuels team: grassland → GR2 and pasture → GR3 in all 20 folds; forest → TU2 in 17.
  • Provisional December setting: round 1's plus ignition from the VIIRS footprint and spread ×0.35. Not validated.
